learning_objective: 🎯 Learn to transform clues, posters, or short notes into well-structured formal letters like Job Applications and Letters to the Editor!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Exams provide verbal (a short paragraph) or visual (a chart/poster) clues. You must understand the core issue from these clues and expand them logically in your letter.
Written to highlight a social issue. Remember: The editor is NOT a problem solver; they just print news. Request them to publish your views to awaken the authorities.

Has two parts: 1. The Cover Letter (applying for the job). 2. The Bio-data/Resume (Personal details, qualifications, experience, and references). Always write 'Encl: Bio-data' at the end of the letter.
Sender's Address -> Date -> Receiver's Address -> Subject (4-6 words) -> Salutation (Sir/Madam) -> Body (3 paragraphs) -> Subscription (Yours sincerely/truly) -> Signature.
Para 1: Introduction (Who are you and why are you writing?). Para 2: Detail/Main Content (Causes, effects, your inputs). Para 3: Conclusion/Action required.

fun_activity.title: 📰 Be the Editor
fun_activity.instructions: Find a newspaper. Look at the 'Letters to the Editor' section. Notice how every letter starts by referring to an issue and ends with a hope that authorities will take action.

exam_tips: 📌 For Job Applications, always draft the Bio-data on a fresh page or draw a box around it to make it stand out.
📌 Keep the Subject very brief. E.g., 'Subject: Application for the post of PGT English'.
📌 Never ask the Editor to fix the pothole or arrest the thief. Ask them to 'highlight the issue in their esteemed column'.
quick_recap: ⭐ Always stick to the formal format; marks are awarded specifically for format.
⭐ Use the exact name and address provided in the question's verbal input.
⭐ 'Yours faithfully' or 'Yours sincerely' is correct. Never write 'Your's'.
